attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The route still lacks a nonlarge, nonconstructive, proof-mediated, or direct argument that the actual SAT label avoids the easy induced-XOR label set.
steps: Model the XOR carrier as a linear map from formula-label vectors y over U_N to N-input truth tables H_N^y.
Assume a certificate property P_N contains y_N^{SAT} and excludes every y with C(H_N^y)<=S_N.
Pull P_N back to a property of all L_N-bit Boolean functions by testing only the coordinates in U_N; density is preserved exactly under random restriction.
If an L_N-bit function f has circuits of size L_N^c, substituting that circuit into the generator computes H_N^f in size N^{max{q,rho}+o(1)}<S_N.
Therefore the pullback property rejects every SIZE(L_N^c) function but accepts SAT, and if it is constructive and large it is a natural property useful against polynomial-size circuits at length L_N.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: This proves a valid obstruction for a certificate method and preserves the beta=0 magnification bridge; it does not prove C(H_N^{SAT})>S_N or P != NP.

assumptions: Circuit model is nonuniform fan-in-two Boolean SIZE; all hidden factors are poly(L_N) or polylogarithmic in N.
P_N is decidable from the truth table on U_N within time poly(2^{L_N}) after reading the relevant labels.
The restriction of a uniformly random L_N-bit Boolean function to U_N is uniform over {0,1}^{U_N}.
The naturalness diagnosis is conditional on standard pseudorandom-function-in-P/poly assumptions; it is a route obstruction, not a proof of P != NP.
For each fixed c, N is large enough that L_N^c=N^{o(1)} and N^{max{q,rho}+o(1)}<N^{1+epsilon}.
definitions: source object: H_N^{SAT}(x)=parity_{j<=Q_N} SAT(G_N(x,j)), with x in {0,1}^N, Q_N=N^q, L_N=(log N)^d, d>1, and U_N the set of L_N-bit formulas generated by G_N.
target object: SAT on L_N-bit formula encodings; the target consequence is SAT notin SIZE(L_N^c) for each fixed c, hence an NP not subset P/poly route only through the beta=0 all-c bridge.

controlled interface: a label-space property P_N subseteq {0,1}^{U_N} containing y_N^{SAT}=SAT restricted to U_N and disjoint from labels y whose induced XOR function H_N^y has circuits of size at most S_N=N^{1+epsilon}.

target-preserving condition: G_N is label-free and computable with overhead N^rho, q<1+epsilon, rho<1+epsilon, beta=0 because L_N=N^{o(1)}, and no nonuniform advice about SAT labels is leaked into G_N or P_N.
A_N is the incidence matrix with row a_x in F_2^{U_N}; H_N^y(x)=<a_x,y>_2.
A lifted property on L_N-bit Boolean functions is \hat P_N(F)=P_N(F restricted to U_N).

attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The missing theorem is not the transfer H(TT(SAT))=>lower bound; it is an unconditional way to establish H_{m,m^k}(TT(SAT_m)) without inducing a large constructive useful property or leaking the target through advice.
steps: Fix m, N=2^m, a finite Boolean basis B, and threshold s=s(m). Define H_{m,s}(y)=1 iff no B-circuit of size at most s computes y.
Count circuit descriptions: at most 2^{c_B s log s} size-s circuits exist, so at most that many N-bit truth tables are excluded from H_{m,s}. Hence H_{m,s} has density 1-2^{c_B s log s-N}.
Usefulness is exact: if H_{m,s}(TT(SAT_m)) holds, then no size-s circuit computes SAT_m on the m-bit slice.
Constructivity by the obvious algorithm costs N^{O(1)}2^{c_B s log s}; it is poly(N) when s log s=O(m), but not by enumeration for s=m^k with k>=1 except sublinear/log thresholds.

Therefore the canonical exact-MCSP property is already a valid natural property at very low thresholds, while polynomial lower-bound thresholds require either a non-enumerative poly(N) recognizer or a nonconstructive/proof-mediated escape.
If a non-enumerative recognizer exists and H_{m,s} remains useful against the same SIZE_m(s), the route conflicts with exponentially secure PRFs in that class by the natural-proofs tuple.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: This is valid route-level progress only. It neither proves SAT lower bounds nor proves PRFs exist; it gives a falsifier for direct exact-MCSP/natural-property routes that claim polynomial thresholds while remaining dense and constructible.

assumptions: Model: nonuniform fanin-2 Boolean circuits over a fixed finite complete basis; size counts gates and input literals are free up to the standard encoding constant.
Regime: N=2^m and s log s=o(N), so the set of size-s truth tables is a vanishing fraction of all N-bit strings.
Uniformity cutoff: natural-proof constructivity is time N^{O(1)} on the full truth table, not time polynomial in m and not an oracle for MCSP.
Barrier condition: the PRF conflict is conditional on exponentially secure pseudorandom functions computable within the same target class SIZE_m(s) or a clearly embedded subclass.
Non-claim boundary: this does not rule out a nonconstructive proof that TT(SAT_m) lies in H_{m,s}; it only audits routes that induce an efficiently recognizable dense property.
definitions: source object: H_{m,s} subset {0,1}^{N}, N=2^m, the exact high-circuit-complexity truth-table property H_{m,s}(y)=1 iff CC_m(y)>s for a fixed fanin-2 Boolean basis.
target object: SAT_m truth table lower bound SAT_m notin SIZE_m(s), with s=m^k or more generally s=s(m) measured on the unpadded m-bit input length.
controlled interface: membership H_{m,s}(TT(SAT_m)) is the carrier, and constructivity is measured by a total algorithm on N-bit truth tables running poly(N).
target-preserving condition: the same input length m, circuit basis, advice convention, and threshold s are used in CC_m, SIZE_m(s), PRF usefulness, and SAT_m.
observable: the barrier-relevant triple is density of H_{m,s}, decision time for H_{m,s}, and usefulness against SIZE_m(s).

attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The derivation still assumes existence of a generated anti-ball source with an unrestricted hard row and with no subthreshold nonuniform skeleton. Proving this source condition may itself require a nonuniform lower bound of comparable strength.
steps: Fix source length m and an accepted row T_{m,a} with claimed CC(T_{m,a})>2^{theta m}.
Assume for contradiction that a skeleton z_{m,a} of length 2^{beta m+o(m)} and a uniform opener O compute T_{m,a}[x] for every m-bit x in time 2^{tau m+o(m)}.
Build a nonuniform circuit for T_{m,a} by hardwiring a and z_{m,a}, then simulating O on input x. The circuit size is 2^{max(beta,tau)m+o(m)}.
If max(beta,tau)<theta, this contradicts the alleged MCSP no-side soundness. Thus every valid generated proof source must be nonuniform-opening-hard at exponent theta.

If no such skeleton exists and some accepted row is genuinely hard, define F_m(a,x)=T_{m,a}[x] over at most 2^{D m+o(m)} ranks. Any circuit for F_m of size below 2^{theta m-o(m)} restricts to a circuit for the hard row by hardwiring a.
Translate input length from m to (1+D)m and then pad across kappa-dense source lengths, giving the conditional E lower-bound exponent delta<theta/(kappa(1+D)).
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: This is valid route-level progress and a falsifier theorem for source proposals, not a proof of P != NP. The construction of the hard generated carrier remains open, and the no-skeleton property is not supplied by natural counting or by dense locators.

assumptions: Source model: truth tables have length N=2^m and MCSP hardness is measured against unrestricted nonuniform Boolean circuits.
Uniformity regime: U_m and the target language evaluator are deterministic and advice-free; per-length advice is allowed only in the falsifier test because MCSP circuits are nonuniform.
Opening regime: a skeleton z_{m,a} may be a proof digest, checkpoint list, Merkle frontier, compressed transcript, or any fixed string from which a uniform decoder opens T_{m,a}[x] for every x.
Density regime: usable source lengths are kappa-dense and D, theta, kappa are fixed constants independent of m.
Barrier regime: the carrier image is sparse and not a large natural property unless a dense projection/locator repair is added.
definitions: source object: a generated anti-ball MCSP carrier C_m=(U_m,A_m,pi_m) on m input bits, where U_m enumerates at most 2^{D m+o(m)} truth-table rows T_{m,a} and generated proof streams pi_{m,a}, and at least one accepted row is claimed to have unrestricted circuit complexity CC(T_{m,a})>2^{theta m}.
target object: an E-uniform multiplexed language L_C whose input of length about (1+D)m encodes a row rank a and an m-bit truth-table address x, with value L_C(a,x)=T_{m,a}[x].

controlled interface: deterministic advice-free unranking and row-bit generation in 2^{O(m)} time, kappa-dense source lengths, and an explicit ledger for any proof projection, checkpoint, digest, or skeleton used to open row bits.

target-preserving condition: every skeleton z that enables indexed openings of an accepted hard row must have combined size/time exponent at least theta-o(1), and the anti-ball soundness statement must exclude unrestricted nonuniform circuits rather than only uniform or restricted decoders.
CC(T) denotes the minimum unrestricted Boolean circuit size of the m-input function with truth table T.
D is the distinct-image entropy rate, so the number of distinct emitted rows is at most 2^{D m+o(m)}.
theta is the source MCSP lower-bound exponent and kappa is the multiplicative source-length gap used for padding to all target lengths.

equations.valid_when: Valid when z is fixed per row or per length, the decoder computes every truth-table bit, and MCSP size is unrestricted nonuniform circuit size.

equations.label: skeleton_falsifier_threshold
equations.valid_when: Valid when the alleged source guarantee claims CC(T_{m,a}) exceeds 2^{theta m} on the same accepted row opened by the skeleton decoder.

equations.label: low_D_multiplex_transfer
equations.valid_when: Valid when source lengths are kappa-dense, distinct row image entropy is Dm+o(m), and any target circuit can be restricted by hardwiring the hard rank.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: Exhibit a subthreshold proof skeleton, checkpoint, digest, or rank/opening advice that lets a uniform decoder compute all bits of an accepted hard row; this falsifier invalidates the source without touching P != NP.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This is a route-specific bridge guard: it preserves the existing carrier-to-E transfer while adding a concrete nonuniform-leakage falsifier for generated proof sources.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Generated anti-ball MCSP carriers transfer to E lower bounds only after a nonuniform proof-skeleton opening audit. If a per-row or per-length skeleton of exponent beta and an opening decoder of exponent tau compute all bits of an alleged hard row with max(beta,tau)<theta, then the MCSP no-side source is falsified; otherwise the usual low-D multiplexing transfer remains conditionally valid.

assumptions: The proof is generated, not existentially searched, so locating it does not cost double-exponential time.
The row-bit generator has a fixed exponential rate; if the rate is unbounded, the target can leave E.
The proof stream is not supplied as nonuniform advice to row-bit circuits unless its supplied projection is counted as a skeleton.
The anti-ball claim is about unrestricted circuits, otherwise the conclusion is only a restricted-class lower bound.

Validity/model regime: this lemma is interpreted only within the stated P vs NP branch model, with the same source object, target object, circuit class, length regime, and advice/uniformity assumptions used by the branch output.
definitions: source object: a deterministic generator emits a row T_{m,a} and possibly a proof stream pi_{m,a} of length 2^{gamma m+o(m)} certifying anti-ball distance from all circuits below 2^{theta m}.
target object: the extracted language is the row-rank multiplexing L_C(a,x)=T_{m,a}[x], not the proof language and not the certificate-search relation.
controlled interface: the target evaluator calls only the row-bit generator or a full sequential row scan in 2^{c m} time for a fixed constant c.
observable: proof length gamma is separated from row-bit latency c and from opening-skeleton exponent max(beta,tau).

equations.label: proof_length_not_in_delta
equations.valid_when: Applies when proof generation is used only to certify source soundness and the target evaluator computes row bits in fixed exponential time without proof advice.

equations.label: fixed_rate_E_membership
equations.valid_when: Valid when the row-bit or sequential row generator has a constant exponential rate after translating n to the source length m.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: If the proof must be searched for, uses per-length advice, has unbounded generation rate, or exposes a subthreshold opening projection, the lemma is not a valid transfer.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This prevents overcharging long generated proofs while keeping the skeleton-opening no-go as the real leakage test.
candidate_lemmas.statement: The length of a generated nonblackbox anti-ball proof is not charged to the E lower-bound exponent, provided row bits are generated advice-free in fixed exponential time and the proof has no subthreshold opening skeleton. Proof length becomes harmful only through locatability, advice, or openings.

assumptions: MCSP no-side soundness requires exclusion of arbitrary nonuniform Boolean circuits of size below 2^{theta m}.
Hardness against uniform algorithms, local decoders, or a restricted algebraic model does not by itself imply unrestricted circuit hardness.
Any reduction from unrestricted circuits to R must be size-preserving up to o(theta m) in the exponent.
definitions: source object: a proof system certifies that T is far from or outside circuits in a named class R, such as formulas, AC0, algebraic circuits, uniform machines, or small decoders.
target object: the intended target is an unrestricted Boolean-circuit lower bound for an E language obtained by MCSP-style extraction.
controlled interface: the bridge from certificate soundness to MCSP soundness must preserve the circuit model, size exponent theta, and nonuniformity.
observable: model mismatch between restricted anti-ball soundness and unrestricted MCSP hardness.

equations.label: model_preservation_requirement
equations.valid_when: Valid when R is a proper restricted class and no explicit size-preserving simulation of unrestricted circuits inside R has been proved.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: Show that the source proof excludes only restricted or uniform objects; then the MCSP carrier transfer is invalid until a size-preserving unrestricted-model bridge is added.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This is a model-identity falsifier for proof-complexity or algebraic anti-ball sources that accidentally certify the wrong lower bound.
candidate_lemmas.statement: An anti-ball certificate against a restricted circuit class R cannot serve as an MCSP no-side carrier unless R contains all unrestricted circuits up to size 2^{theta m} or a separate valid reduction from unrestricted circuits to R is supplied.

falsifiers: falsifier: a proof digest, Merkle frontier, checkpoint list, or compressed transcript of size 2^{beta m} with beta<theta that opens every row bit.
falsifier: an opening algorithm running in 2^{tau m} with tau<theta even if the proof generator is advice-free.
falsifier: the anti-ball proof excludes only uniform machines, local decoders, formulas, AC0, or algebraic circuits rather than unrestricted Boolean circuits.
falsifier: row rank selection uses per-length advice or a nonuniform hard-row choice not encoded in the E-uniform multiplexed language.
falsifier: distinct-image entropy D is unbounded, causing the extracted exponent theta/(kappa(1+D)) to collapse to o(1).
falsifier: dense projection or locator repair makes a polynomial-time decidable useful natural property while preserving small-circuit exclusion.
falsifier: source lengths are not kappa-dense, so the lower bound applies only to sparse lengths and does not transfer to the claimed all-length E target.
